name: Santenay

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Seasons this cool ripen Pinot Noir, Chardonnay, Müller-Thurgau, Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer fully without cooking off their freshness.
Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

soil.rock: Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its pH is close to neutral, so vines take up the nutrients they need easily.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Only very early grapes ripen well, mostly hybrids and a few vinifera.
